clue.text: Alert criminal in court defeat

indicators.note: one part sits in the middle of the other, so the shuffled letters go inside

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the word before it is bent out of its order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A vigilant crook is defeated in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb meaning to woo, and its letters wrap around the shuffled ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final battle gave the language 'meet one's Waterloo', so the name stands for a decisive defeat.

clue.text: Confused, I see, after turning up axes

indicators.note: this word places the expression of understanding behind the letters for the axes
in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: 'ah' is what you say when you see the point
z and y are names for axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Someone muddled realises something after the tools are lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like chopping tools, but here it means the axes of a graph, conventionally labelled with letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazy mind is fuzzy and unclear, which is a near synonym of confused.

clue.text: Male with suitable time to drop round, one going on foot

indicators.note: a round thing is a ring shape, and dropping it means losing that ring-shaped letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
an occasion is a fitting or suitable time

explanation.surface: A man waits for the right moment to pop round to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop round' looks like a social visit; 'round' is the ring-shaped letter O, removed once from the word for a suitable time.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather shoe, so it is something that goes on the foot.

clue.text: Shelters in a yard in poor areas

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the unit of length is placed inside the word for run-down districts

parts.note: slums are poor urban areas
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Homeless shelters set up in a courtyard in a deprived district.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' joins definition to wordplay; the second puts Y inside SLUMS after its S, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum in its older sense is a place of refuge or sanctuary, so asylums are shelters.

clue.text: American, in private, is sillier

indicators.note: the national abbreviation is placed inside the word for private

parts.note: inner thoughts are private ones
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American soldier, a private, is the more foolish of the two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier's rank; here it is an adjective meaning inner.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or foolish, so the comparative inaner means more foolish.

clue.text: Chap sheltered by French 8 is grasping English, history, philosophy, etc

indicators.note: what is sheltered is protected inside something else

parts.note: huit is French for the number eight

indicators.note: a word that grasps something holds it inside

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A man inside a French parasol takes in English, history and philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' looks like a cross-reference to 8 across, but it is just the number eight translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanities are the academic subjects about human culture, of which history and philosophy are examples.

clue.text: Track by lake with, say, sharp bend

parts.note: to dog someone is to track them
L is the abbreviation for lake
eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A path running beside a lake has a hairpin turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' looks like a path, but it is the verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-leg is an abrupt angle in a road or golf hole, so it is a sharp bend.

clue.text: Soldiers welcoming really large protective devices

indicators.note: a host who welcomes guests takes them inside

parts.note: paras are paratroopers
'so' as in 'so good' means really
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Troops receive some very big pieces of protective kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Really large' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces, an adverb and a clothing-size abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, a device for protection against the sun.

clue.text: Felon ultimately with not one regret, going around cell

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of felon

indicators.note: going around turns the words back on themselves

parts.note: no means not a single one
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A remorseless criminal paces round his prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' looks like a prison cell; it is the definition in its biological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell, the basic unit of the nervous system.

clue.text: Tax — it's ignored in frivolity

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: levity is light-hearted frivolity
taken as written: the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Taxation is no laughing matter, being excluded from all fun.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is removed from LEVITY, leaving LEVY.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a charge imposed by authority, the same thing as a tax.

clue.text: How India was once ruled: friend getting behind India

indicators.note: the friend word receives the other parts and so comes after them

parts.note: the colon is part of the bowel, the body's behind
India is I in the NATO alphabet
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A historical comment on British rule in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like 'after', but it is a noun for the backside, giving COLON. India appears twice: once in the definition, once as I.
explanation.definitionFit: India was a British colony, so it was governed colonially, as a dependent territory.

clue.text: Alaskans salute reforms

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it again in a new shape

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: People in Alaska applaud changes to the system.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aleuts are the native people of the Aleutian Islands, which belong to Alaska.

clue.text: Rough quality still maintained by country club head

indicators.note: something maintained is held and kept within, so it goes inside

'even' as in 'even better' means still
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A country club's boss keeps up its rough-and-ready character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' looks like a golf club, but it is the United Nations, a club of countries; 'head' is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Unevenness is the state of not being smooth or level, which is roughness.

clue.text: Pattern spoils clothing man put on board

definitions.note: singular collective noun for the plural answer

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap around it

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
the king is a man, a piece, set on the chessboard

explanation.surface: Bad tailoring spoils the dress of a man joining the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' in chess is any piece; the one set out on the board here is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Markings are the spots and stripes on an animal's coat, which together form its pattern.

clue.text: Respected figure you once introduced to poet

indicators.note: being introduced into something means going inside it

parts.note: John Donne, the metaphysical poet
ye is the old word for you

explanation.surface: A distinguished person, once introduced to a famous poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most senior and respected woman in a field.

clue.text: Running trial as a way to get hold of stock

definitions.note: singular phrase for the plural answer

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Running a test as a method of acquiring shares in the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks financial, but it is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a rope with a noose used to catch cattle.

clue.text: Firm, stable worker admitted to tremendous honour

indicators.note: what is admitted is let in, so it goes inside

parts.note: ace means excellent, tremendous
Co is short for company, a firm
a stable lad looks after racehorses

explanation.surface: A stable hand joins a solid racing firm, a great honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' and 'stable' look like adjectives meaning steady, but they give a company and a racing yard's lad.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise, so it is an honour.

clue.text: NHS working with inert solvents

indicators.note: something being worked is kneaded into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Health service staff use inactive cleaning chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinners are solvents used to dilute paint or varnish.

clue.text: Parent, say, ignoring rule, gets ecstasy

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a parent is an example of a relation
R is the abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: A mum who breaks the house rules gets hold of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecstasy' suggests the drug; here it is great joy. R comes off the front of RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness and exhilaration, which is what ecstasy means.

clue.text: Like certain complaints from Frenchman, back cutting meat

indicators.note: something that cuts into a thing goes inside it

indicators.note: going back means reading the name in the opposite direction

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's back trouble from cutting meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Venereal describes diseases passed on through sexual contact, a certain class of complaints.

clue.text: Periodically set up sex session for Farage once?

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of these words
a romp is a bout of sex in tabloid slang

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about a sex scandal staged for Nigel Farage.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is a British politician who sat in the European Parliament until Brexit. 'Set up' looks like 'arranged'; its alternate letters give EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Farage was formerly a Member of the European Parliament, which is a Euro-MP.

clue.text: Inter's B Team leaving area on ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade
something leaving goes away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter' looks like the Italian football club; it is the verb meaning bury. A leaves B TEAM, and what remains is shuffled with ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter someone is to bury them, and to entomb is to place a body in a tomb.

clue.text: Seize an advantage from what each other across answer has

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Gewürztraminer is an aromatic white wine; emptied of its middle it is just GR.

clue.text: Drinker of cool old whiskey to start with
